Nothing changes your files until you say so

Reading is free. Writing to a model, sending a mail or spending stops at one Approve card. After you approve, ArchHub reads the real file again to confirm.

  2. ApproveOne card names exactly what will change. Approve, ask why, or reject.
  3. ConfirmThe result is re-read from the real Revit file, mailbox or folder.

Before you install

Does it cost anything?

No. ArchHub is free during beta. You pay only the model provider you choose, on your own account with them. Plans

Do I need administrator rights?

No. It installs for your Windows user only, into your own app data folder.

Will it change my Revit or AutoCAD files?

Not by itself. Reading is free; any write stops at an Approve card that names what will change. Security

Does my work leave my PC?

Only when a step you approved calls a model or a service you chose. Your files stay on your PC. Privacy

Do I need an account?

No. The canvas, files and connectors work signed out. A free account adds cloud models and your office. Create one

How do I remove it?

Start menu, Uninstall ArchHub. Your .archhub files stay where you saved them.

pages./docs/getting-started:
Docs / Getting started

Getting started

ArchHub is a Windows desktop app. This page covers the installer, the first open, signing in and updates.

Install

  1. Download the Windows installer from the Download page.
  2. Run it. It installs for your Windows user only, into %LOCALAPPDATA%\ArchHub, without administrator rights.
  3. ArchHub needs Python 3.11 or newer. If setup cannot find it, it downloads Python for your user only, without changing your PATH.
  4. Setup adds ArchHub and Uninstall ArchHub to the Start menu.

First open

The first time, a setup window prepares the build: a private Python environment, a load check, and a list of the design programs it finds, without opening any of them. When it is ready the app opens.

If a step fails, the window prints the reason and stays open. Keep that text when you report a problem.

Use it in ArchHub

Home, choose a starter, then Start. Start places the wired nodes on the canvas. It does not run them.

Sign in

Open Settings, Account, Continue with Google. Your browser finishes the sign-in and the app updates by itself. The website has no sign-in form. What the account does.

pages./features:
What ArchHub does

Blocks wired together on a canvas, saved as files you can share. You, your agents and your design programs work on the same canvas.

Everything is a node

Every step is a node with typed sockets and parameters. Wire them; change a value and the pure nodes downstream solve again at once.

Runs only when you press Run

Anything that writes a file, changes a host model, sends or spends waits for Run, and for your yes where your setting asks for it.

One file per piece of work

A canvas is one .archhub file. Save, open, copy and share it like any document. Opening a file never runs it.

Any agent on your PC

Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and Goose use the same canvas tools you do. No vendor lock.

Inside your programs

Host nodes read and write Revit, AutoCAD, Excel and Outlook through connectors on your PC.

Skills you save become nodes

Group nodes, save the group as a skill, and it appears in the Library as one node for you and every agent.

The canvas and the composer
pages./security:
Security

Your own agents work freely in your registered folders. The edges that matter always stop for your yes, whatever the agent or vendor.

What always asks you first

Send or publish

Email, posts and anything that reaches other people.

Write to a host model

Changes to a live Revit or AutoCAD file.

Client data

Nothing marked client or private goes to the public or a model without you.

Spend

Anything that costs money.

How it is built

Secrets
Keys and tokens live in Windows Credential Manager. Never in a .archhub file, a setting, a log, a model prompt or a URL.
Files
Opening a file never runs it. Saving is atomic: a failed write keeps the old file.
Identity
Your account is your email, not your machine.
Connectors
Each host connector allows a listed set of actions. Unknown actions are refused.
Model output
Text from a model or a web page cannot change a rule or run an effect by itself.

Report a security problem

Do not post it in public. Use GitHub's private report on the repository.

Properties, shared parameters and classification

Worksets, model checks, naming and new parameters for every project model.

Rules

  • One file only: new parameters are added to BA-SHARED_PARAMETERS.txt by the BIM team, never a second file.
  • A parameter keeps its GUID for life. Never delete and re-create one with the same name: Revit treats it as a different parameter.
  • Name it for what it holds, in the group of its discipline (00.GENERAL, 01.SHEETS&VIEWS, 02.OPENINGS). The meaning, data type, unit and owner are recorded in the BA-STD-72 workbook.
  • Worksets are named BA-<discipline>-<element>, for example BA-A-WAL, BA-S-CLM, BA-M-DCT.

Worksets and model checks

  1. Collaborate, Worksets to enable worksharing. Then run BA-DYN-CREATE-WORKSETS-NO-PACKAGE-v02.dyn: it renames Workset1 to Core, Modeling and creates the other worksets.
  2. Install the BIM Interoperability Tools. In Revit: Model Checker, Setup, open BA-QA-MODEL-CHECK.xml, then Run.
Use it in ArchHub

Ask BABOOM “check the shared parameters in this model”, or place the Model check node from Library, Office library (BABOOM).

Downloads: BA-SHARED-PARAMETERS-GUIDE.pdf · needs a free ArchHub account

docs: Nodes, typed wires, properties, runs and composer drafts.
The canvas holds your work: nodes, the wires between them and their properties.
The composer drafts changes to the canvas from a request you type. A model draft stays inert until you press Run.
The Node library is the one catalogue for placeable nodes.
Open a .archhub file from Home, or start a new canvas.
Every agent and you in one room.
The Workshop is the one room where you and every agent work together.
Work sits on the left: every task, grouped as Needs attention and In progress. Show history adds Completed and archived. Click a task to open it.
Home, then any piece of work: its thread is the Workshop for that work.
One agent per task, so no work is done twice.
A task is one job in the Workshop.
When an agent takes a task, it is claimed: it shows as Working, under In progress, with that agent’s name, and no other agent can take it.
An agent holds a task for 15 minutes at a time and renews it while it works. If it goes quiet, the hold runs out and the task is free for the next agent.
Home: each row shows the agents on that work.
Approvals: how much agents may do without asking
One setting decides when an agent asks you first.
Accept edits (the default): agents work without prompting you.
Ask first: an agent asks you before it deletes, publishes or sends anything, and before it changes anything outside your own folders.
Plan only: agents may read and plan, but every change waits for you.
Routines: work that runs by itself
A Schedule or File change node runs a workflow and reports back.
A routine is a workflow with a trigger node at its start.
On the canvas, add a Schedule node (runs at the times you set) or a File change node (runs when a file in a folder changes).
Wire it to the nodes it should run and save the workflow. While ArchHub is open, the routine fires by itself.
Host programs, what each node needs, and what is available.
The connector table comes from the operation catalogue and the release’s host artifact index.
A packaged connector is not a running connection. Open the host program with its connector loaded before using its nodes.
Sign in with your email account, sign out, and what needs one.
An ArchHub account is an email address, not a machine. Sign in on another computer with the same email and it is the same account.
In the app open Settings, Account, then Continue with Google.
Local memory and what sharing does in this build.
